notes:
Passed on the fake backend only by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware backend exists or was run and no real ROS or hardware claim is made. The card's mock_strategy.preferred upstream-sim was not used: the clone is read-only and is never imported or executed, and its MuJoCo/dm_control/mojo stack and assets were not installed. fake.py is therefore an analytic F0 task-level stand-in, not a recording and not the upstream simulator; no recorded traffic is replayed. Configuration assumed: the default H1 robot with JointPositionActionMode(floating_base=True, absolute=False), Robotiq 2F85 grippers and control_frequency 500 Hz. The fake's action Box has 15 values (3 floating-base, 10 arm/wrist, 2 grippers) and uses the upstream default bounds; the real space is built from the loaded model and the constructor action mode, so other action modes, floating-DOF sets, robots, control frequencies or gripper configurations change shape and bounds. The driver sets no Limit and no action_space_ref because no single upstream line states all 15 bounds; the reference marks the derived action limits with their origin, the fake backend, and not with a source. The fake's observation arrays are shorter than upstream's: 4 proprioception values instead of len(robot.qpos)+len(robot.qvel), 2 gripper values, and 3 floating-base position and accumulated-action values (the default H1 X/Y/RZ configuration); the real lengths depend on the model and action mode. Truncation, the simulation health monitor, contacts, actuators, sensors, camera/depth/privileged observations and rendering are not modelled, and the sim backend is not declared. Expected warnings in the last gate run: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the bridge's seed class only records the next reset seed and makes no native call; the fake would otherwise have nothing to call) and four G8.NO_UNIT warnings for the bridge-derived integer inputs (ticks, seed twice) and the simulator action array; there are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. test_driver.py keeps the check_driver call and adds cases for the fake Box bounds, the observation stand-in, reset/seed handling, reset options, the DrawerTopOpen success termination, the 10 m failure termination, the fidelity contract and the e-stop latch. gate.digest is the digest the last check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the Gymnasium package against the readiness evidence (repairable: GymnasiumDriver over a directly constructed DrawerTopOpen), which it matches, and against the source: DrawerTopOpen (bigym/envs/cupboards.py:34-38) is a BiGymEnv (bigym/bigym_env.py:34); the fake's 15-value Box equals the default H1 JointPositionActionMode bounds (DEFAULT_DOFS X, Y, RZ at action_modes.py:39; h1.py:126-127, 147; robotiq.py:10; action_scale 1 at 500 Hz, bigym_env.py:96-98, 106-108), and the reference marks those step bounds as the fake's, without a source; success, failure, reward, termination, the fast step and the bounds check follow bigym_env.py:420-496, and every fact matches its lines. No sim backend is declared, so the package is accepted as a fake-only contract under the simulator policy, with its gaps in the fidelity block; not listed there: the fake adds the current floating-base action to the accumulated-action observation, while upstream adds the previous one (bigym/robots/floating_base.py:111-114, 182-184). Licence finding: the README lists CC BY-NC 4.0 among the 3D asset licences (README.md:153-156; the Box asset, bigym/envs/xmls/3D_MODELS_ATTRIBUTION.md:52-57) while the card says Apache-2.0 with publish_review not_required; the override proposal adds publish_review required and must be merged by hand into the existing robots.json entry. No package file was changed (the gate re-run only regenerated check-report.json); the gate and collect.py --strict pass (sha256:73e8ab2e3ae745e3673cb372026aad73c5f0613622a7d8866464945df8f519d7). For the human reviewer: Simulation only. env_id 'bigym:DrawerTopOpen' is a label: BiGym registers no Gymnasium ids (tasks are instantiated directly, README.md:82), so a sim backend built from it would fail; a future sim factory must construct DrawerTopOpen with an explicit action mode.
